coding_context.description: Input, Process, and Output Anxiety Scales predict general language learning anxiety
coding_context.reported_success_quote:
In both the initial as well as the replication study, evidence showed
that language learners experience significantly higher levels of output anxiety than
input or process anxiety; nonetheless, these three types of anxiety were found to be
linked to the general concept of language anxiety to different degrees, with process
anxiety depicting the strongest association according to the results of data analysis
in the initial and the replication study.
Although the scales could be characterized as reliable, their componential struc-
ture was found to be not without flaws. Some of the same items of the scales were
labelled as problematic in the Hungarian version of the scales as well as in the English
version. As such, it can be said that these issues are inherent to the items rather than
to their translated versions and thus warrant reconsideration.

prior_adjudication.quote: These results suggest that anxiety experienced at the processing stage has a more significant effect on general language anxiety than anxiety experienced at the output stage of language learning, which is also consistent with Onwuegbuzie et al.’s (2000) findings.
